## Prepare for the analysis

### Define essential parameters

Set the year, where the data should begin with 1980. Currently the latest report go until 2030. We assume afterwards a constant composition.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

startDate <- 1980

```

# Developement of the car weight

## Show the developemt and anlyse it

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.show='hold'}

# Get the long format to use ggplot

carWeight_long <- carWeight %>% select(-SegmentAMass) %>% pivot_longer(cols = -Year, names_to = 'Segment', values_to = 'values')

# Display the different car weights per segment over time

ggplot() +
      geom_point(data = carWeight_long, mapping = aes(x = Year, y = values, colour = Segment)) +
      geom_smooth(data = carWeight_long, mapping = aes(x = Year, y = values, colour = Segment), method = "loess", se = FALSE) +
      ggtitle("Car weight based on common types") +
      scale_x_continuous(name = "year") +
      scale_y_continuous(name = "mass per vehicle (kg)")

# Display standard cars

carWeight_long %>% filter(Segment == "StandardMass") %>%
    ggplot(mapping = aes(x = Year, y = values)) +
      geom_point() +
      geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE) +
      ggtitle("Standard car weight based on common types") +
      scale_x_continuous(name = "year")
      scale_y_continuous(name = "mass per vehicle (kg)")

# Display standard cars from 1980 t0 2010

carWeight_long %>% filter((Segment == "StandardMass") & (Year >= 1980) & (Year <= 2010)) %>%
    ggplot(mapping = aes(x = Year, y = values)) +
      geom_point() +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
      ggtitle("Standard car weight based on common types") +
      scale_x_continuous(name = "year")
      scale_y_continuous(name = "mass per vehicle (kg)")
      
# Model the car weight
      
carWeightStandard <- carWeight_long %>% filter((Segment == "StandardMass") & (Year >= 1980) & (Year <= 2010))

modelcarWeightStandard <- lm(values ~ Year, data = carWeightStandard)
summary(modelcarWeightStandard)

# Create a new data frame with the year you want to interpolate
start_value <- data.frame(Year = 1980)
end_value <- data.frame(Year = 2010)

# Use the predict function to get the interpolated value
startWeightCar <- predict(modelcarWeightStandard, newdata = start_value)
endWeightCar <- predict(modelcarWeightStandard, newdata = end_value)
      
```


# Alumnium content

## aluminum table 1

The file filename1_inputs <- "Data/1_VehicleCompositionNewData.xlsx" with the sheet "aluminum_content_1" is based on the following report and data. 'Aluminum Content in Passenger Vehicles (Europe) Assessment 2022 and Outlook 2026, 2030 - Public Summary - April, 2023 (2023_04_Aluminum-Content_Ducker-Study_EA-Public-Summary_190423.pdf) page 26. It has been derived from the numbers in the figure and the comments.

## aluminum table 2

The file filename1_inputs <- "Data/1_VehicleCompositionNewData.xlsx" with the sheet "aluminum_content_2" is based on the following report and data.'Aluminum Content in Passenger Vehicles (Europe) Assessment 2022 and Outlook 2026, 2030 - Public Summary - April, 2023 (2023_04_Aluminum-Content_Ducker-Study_EA-Public-Summary_190423.pdf) page 13. It has been derived from the numbers in the figure and the comments.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# add the total weight

aluminum_content_1 <- aluminum_content_1 %>% group_by(year) %>% mutate(total = SheetAluminum + ExtrusionAluminum + CastingAluminum + ForgingAluminum)

# generate a long format

aluminum_content_1 <- aluminum_content_1 %>% pivot_longer(!year, names_to = "material", values_to = "mass")

aluminum_content_2 <- aluminum_content_2 %>% filter(scenario == "base")

## display as a figure

g <- ggplot() +
      geom_point(data = aluminum_content_1, mapping = aes(x = year, y = mass, colour = material)) +
      geom_point(data = aluminum_content_2, mapping = aes(x = year, y = totalMass), colour = "green") +
      geom_smooth(data = aluminum_content_2, mapping = aes(x = year, y = totalMass), method = "loess", se = FALSE, linetype = "dashed", colour = "green") +
      ggtitle("aluminum data (content 1 & 2 (green))") +
      scale_y_continuous(name = "mass per vehicle (kg)") +
      coord_fixed(ratio = 0.05)  # Adjust the ratio as needed

plot(g)

```

## aluminum content 4 

### 2020 data

The file filename1_inputs <- "Data/1_VehicleCompositionNewData.xlsx" with the sheet "aluminum_content_4" the 2020 are based on the "2020 North America light vehicle aluminum content and outlook - Final report summary (July 2020)" (DuckerFrontier-Aluminum-Association-2020-Content-Study-Summary-Report-FINAL.pdf) page 12.

### 2023 data

The second set of data comes from "Light vehicle aluminum content and outlook study - prepared for the aluminum association by Ducker April 2023 (Ducker-ATG-2023-Summary-Report-April-2023.pdf) page 13.

### Conversion of all data from lb to kg

New rows are added to the data.frame with the kg values. The conversion factor is: x lb * 0.45359237 = y kg

## aluminum content 5 

### 2020 data

The file filename1_inputs <- "Data/1_VehicleCompositionNewData.xlsx" with the sheet "aluminum_content_5" the 2020 are based on the "2020 North America light vehicle aluminum content and outlook - Final report summary (July 2020)" (DuckerFrontier-Aluminum-Association-2020-Content-Study-Summary-Report-FINAL.pdf) page 13.

### 2023 data

The second set of data comes from "Light vehicle aluminum content and outlook study - prepared for the aluminum association by Ducker April 2023 (Ducker-ATG-2023-Summary-Report-April-2023.pdf) page 16.

### Conversion of all data from lb to kg

New rows are added to the data.frame with the kg values. The conversion factor is: x lb * 0.45359237 = y kg


```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

lbTokg <- 0.45359237

# aluminum_content_4
aluminum_content_4$Content2023 <- aluminum_content_4$`AluminumContent (lb) - 2023` * lbTokg
aluminum_content_4$Content2020 <- aluminum_content_4$`AluminumContent (lb) - 2020` * lbTokg
#aluminum_content_4

# aluminum_content_5
aluminum_content_5$SheetAluminum <- aluminum_content_5$`SheetAluminum (lb)` * lbTokg
aluminum_content_5$ExtrusionAluminum <- aluminum_content_5$`ExtrusionAluminum (lb)` * lbTokg
aluminum_content_5$CastingAluminum <- aluminum_content_5$`CastingAluminum (lb)` * lbTokg
aluminum_content_5$ForgingAluminum <- aluminum_content_5$`ForgingAluminum (lb)` * lbTokg
aluminum_content_5$Total <- aluminum_content_5$`Total (lb)` * lbTokg
#aluminum_content_5

# transform aluminum_content_5 to long format with kg values

aluminum_content_5_long <- aluminum_content_5 %>% pivot_longer(cols = c(SheetAluminum, ExtrusionAluminum, CastingAluminum, ForgingAluminum, Total), names_to = "materials", values_to = "mass")

#aluminum_content_5_long
```

### Interpolate the values from 1980 to 2030 for totalaluminum for a standard car (V0101010000)

In a first step the total amount of aluminum used in a standard car are interpolated for each year using all the available data.For this purpose a loess fiting procedure in R is used. This allows to obtain the values for each year in the time span from 1980 to 2030. 

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# get the old data and generate long table for the interpolation
aluminum_content_4_long <- aluminum_content_4 %>% pivot_longer(cols = c("Content2023", "Content2020"), names_to = "study",
                                                                 values_to = "values", values_drop_na = TRUE)
#aluminum_content_4_long

# model the data
yearCalculate <- c(1975:2030)
yearCalculate <- as.integer(yearCalculate)

mAltotal <- loess(values ~ year, data = aluminum_content_4_long, span = 0.85)
valueCalulate <- predict(mAltotal, yearCalculate)
temp <- valueCalulate  # this is necessary, but I have no idea why

totalAlCaluclate.standard <- data.frame(cbind(year = yearCalculate, value = temp))
totalAlCaluclate.standard <- totalAlCaluclate.standard %>% add_column(segment = "standard")
#totalAlCaluclate.standard

# the data are shown in a figure with the interpolated vaules as a point and the loess function as a dashed line

g <- ggplot() +
      geom_point(data = totalAlCaluclate.standard, mapping = aes(x = year, y = value), color = "blue") +
      geom_smooth(data = totalAlCaluclate.standard, mapping = aes(x = year, y = value), method = "loess", se = FALSE,
                  linetype = "dashed", colour = "blue") +
      ggtitle("Total of all aluminum alloys in a standard car (interpolated)") +
      xlab("production year") +
      ylab("mass (kg) per car") +
      coord_fixed(ratio = 0.13)  # Adjust the ratio as needed

plot(g)

# Start with 1980

totalAlCaluclate.standard <- totalAlCaluclate.standard %>% filter(year >= startDate)
#totalAlCaluclate.standard

```


### Interpolate the values from 1980 to 2030 for extrusion, forging and sheet aluminum alloys (wrought aluminum) for a standard car (V0101010000)

The different type of wrought Aluminum productions are looked for their amounts in standard cars over the investigated time period. The issue is, that there are hardly any numbers before the year 2015 for the different types. Only the overall wrought aluminum is listed in older studies.

#### Extrusion aluminum

The available data points are best modeled with a linear regression. Therefore it seems appropriated to extend the linear model approach for the years before 2016, where the first data are available. Using this linear approach the extrusion values become 0 before the year 2005, which seems reasonable.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

yearCalculate <- c(startDate:2030)

# model the values

mAlExtrusion <- lm(ExtrusionAluminum ~ year, data = aluminum_content_5)
#summary(mAlExtrusion)

valueCalculate <- yearCalculate * mAlExtrusion$coefficients[2] + mAlExtrusion$coefficients[1]
extrusionAlCalculate.standard <- data.frame(cbind(year = yearCalculate, value = valueCalculate))
extrusionAlCalculate.standard <- extrusionAlCalculate.standard %>% add_column(segment = "standard")

# get ride of all values < 0
extrusionAlCalculate.standard <- extrusionAlCalculate.standard %>% mutate(value = if_else(value < 0, 0, value))
#extrusionAlCalculate.standard

g <- ggplot() +
      geom_point(data = aluminum_content_5, mapping = aes(x = year, y = ExtrusionAluminum)) +
      geom_smooth(data = aluminum_content_5, mapping = aes(x = year, y = ExtrusionAluminum), method='lm', se = FALSE) +
      geom_point(data = extrusionAlCalculate.standard, mapping = aes(x = year, y = value), colour = "blue") +
      ggtitle("Extrusion aluminum alloys for standard car (linear model)") +
      xlab("production year") +
      ylab("mass (kg) per car") +
      coord_fixed(ratio = 0.5)  # Adjust the ratio as needed

plot(g)

```


#### Forgingaluminum

The available data points are best modeled with a linear regression. Therefore it seems appropriated to extend the linear model approach for the years before 2016, where the first data are available. Using this linear approach the extrusion values become 0 before the year 2003, which seems reasonable.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

yearCalculate <- c(startDate:2030)

# model the values

mAlForging <- lm(ForgingAluminum ~ year, data = aluminum_content_5)
#summary(mAlForging)

valueCalculate <- yearCalculate * mAlForging$coefficients[2] + mAlForging$coefficients[1]
forgingAlCaluclate.standard <- data.frame(cbind(year = yearCalculate, value = valueCalculate))
forgingAlCaluclate.standard <- forgingAlCaluclate.standard %>% add_column(segment = "standard")

# get ride of all values < 0
forgingAlCaluclate.standard <- forgingAlCaluclate.standard %>% mutate(value = if_else(value < 0, 0, value))
#forgingAlCaluclate.standard

g <- ggplot() +
      geom_point(data = aluminum_content_5, mapping = aes(x = year, y = ForgingAluminum)) +
      geom_smooth(data = aluminum_content_5, mapping = aes(x = year, y = ForgingAluminum), method='lm', se = FALSE) +
      geom_point(data = forgingAlCaluclate.standard, mapping = aes(x = year, y = value), colour = "blue") +
      ggtitle("Forging aluminum alloys for standard car (linear model)") +
      xlab("production year") +
      ylab("mass (kg) per car") +
      coord_fixed(ratio = 5.0)  # Adjust the ratio as needed

plot(g)

```

#### Sheetaluminum

The available data points are best modeled with a linear regression. Therefore it seems appropriated to extend the linear model approach for the years before 2016, where the first data are available. Using this linear approach the extrusion values become 0 before the year 2000, which seems reasonable.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

```

The JRC data show some small amounts of wrought aluminum in cars. The amount is below 20 kg. According to the article "Automotive Aluminum Challenges Steel -
As aluminum manufacturers keep pushing for increased market share in automotive design and content, their efforts may create some changes on the recycling end." (https://www.recyclingtoday.com/article/automotive-aluminum-challenges-steel/), which was published in August 2001, aluminum has grown slowly to about 12% of the car weight. This is mainly cast aluminum, whereas wrought aluminum application were just introduced for the E and F segment type of cars.


### castaluminum for a standard car ("V0101010000") based on the total amount of aluminum and wrought (forging, extrusion & sheet) aluminum from 1980 - 2030

There is a extended data set for the whole amount of aluminum in cars and also the amount of the wrought aluminum are know and modeled. The amount of cast aluminum is the difference between the two values. This can be verified with independent data for cast aluminum.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# get the total data
castingAlCalculate.standard <- totalAlCaluclate.standard %>% mutate(value = value - extrusionAlCalculate.standard$value - forgingAlCaluclate.standard$value - sheetAlCaluclate.standard$value)
#castingAlCalculate.standard

# plot the results
g <- ggplot() +
      geom_point(data = castingAlCalculate.standard, mapping = aes(x = year, y = value), colour = "blue") +
      geom_smooth(data = castingAlCalculate.standard, mapping = aes(x = year, y = value), method = "loess", se = FALSE, span = 0.4) +
      ggtitle("Casting aluminum alloys for standard car (smooth loess model)") +
      xlab("production year") +
      ylab("mass (kg) per car") +
      coord_fixed(ratio = 0.3)  # Adjust the ratio as needed

plot(g)

# Check casting aluminum to total weight in 1980 and 2010
castingAlCalculate.standard_1980 <- castingAlCalculate.standard %>% filter(year == 1980)
castingAlCalculate.standard_2010 <- castingAlCalculate.standard %>% filter(year == 2010)

# Calculate the ratio
ratiocastingAl_1980 <- castingAlCalculate.standard_1980$value / startWeightCar
ratiocastingAl_2010 <- castingAlCalculate.standard_2010$value / startWeightCar

#ratiocastingAl_1980
#ratiocastingAl_2010
```

The smooth line does not represent the individual values for each year. It is just an approximation of the individual values shown as points and which are used.

Testing the increase in ratio of casting Al from 1980 from 4.6% to 11.5% in 2010 is in line with the overall weight increase. Therefore it is justified to not use the old JRC data, as they do not reflect the actual behavior over this timeperiod. Furthermore, they also ignors that a standard car weight increase between 19080 and 2010 by 17 kg per year.

## Combination of all aluminum Alloys into one file and figure (1980 - 2030)

### Combined data set of a standard car (1980 - 2030)

All the data of the different aluminum alloys are combined into one single data set. Currently there are only the data of the standard car, which is an average car between an C and D segment car. 

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# combining the data

AlCalculate.standard <- left_join(castingAlCalculate.standard, extrusionAlCalculate.standard, by = c("year", "segment"))
AlCalculate.standard <- left_join(AlCalculate.standard, forgingAlCaluclate.standard, by = c("year", "segment"))
AlCalculate.standard <- left_join(AlCalculate.standard, sheetAlCaluclate.standard, by = c("year", "segment"))

# renaming some of the columns

AlCalculate.standard <- AlCalculate.standard %>% rename("castingValue" = "value.x", "extrusionValue" = "value.y",
                                                              "forgingValue" = "value.x.x", "sheetValue" = "value.y.y")

# calculate the total amount of aluminum in the data set

AlCalculate.standard <- AlCalculate.standard %>% mutate(combinedValue = castingValue + extrusionValue + forgingValue + sheetValue)

# do some rearrangement of the data set structure

AlCalculate.standard <- AlCalculate.standard %>% relocate(segment, .after = last_col())
#AlCalculate.V0101010000

# generate long table, so that all the data in the data set can be shown in a figue

AlCalculate.standard_long <- AlCalculate.standard %>% pivot_longer(!c(year, segment), names_to = "AlAlloys", values_to = "values")
#AlCalculate.V0101010000_long

g <- ggplot() +
      geom_point(data = AlCalculate.standard_long, mapping = aes(x = year, y = values, color = AlAlloys)) +
      geom_smooth(data = AlCalculate.standard_long, mapping = aes(x = year, y = values, color = AlAlloys), method = "loess", se = FALSE) +
      ggtitle("aluminum alloys for standard car - Comparison with study") +
      xlab("production year") +
      ylab("mass (kg) per car") +
      coord_fixed(ratio = 0.15)  # Adjust the ratio as needed

plot(g)

AlCalculate.standard_long <- AlCalculate.standard %>% pivot_longer(!c(year, segment), names_to = "AlAlloys", values_to = "values")
#AlCalculate.V0101010000_long

temp <-AlCalculate.standard_long

temp$AlAlloys <- factor(temp$AlAlloys,
                                 levels = c("castingValue", "extrusionValue", "forgingValue", "sheetValue", "combinedValue"),
                                 labels = c("cast aluminum", "extrusion aluminum", "forging aluminum", "sheet aluminum", "total"))


g <- ggplot() +
      geom_point(data = temp, mapping = aes(x = year, y = values, color = AlAlloys)) +
      geom_smooth(data = temp, mapping = aes(x = year, y = values, color = AlAlloys), method = "loess", se = FALSE) +
      ggtitle("Aluminum Alloys for std. Car") +
      xlab("production year") +
      ylab("mass (kg) per car") +
      coord_fixed(ratio = 0.15) + # Adjust the ratio as needed
      scale_color_discrete(name = "aluminum alloys") +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),  # Remove major grid lines
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),  # Remove minor grid lines
      text = element_text(size = 15),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 15, color = "black"),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold"),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
)

plot(g)

ggsave("Data/Figure05.png", g, 
       width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")




```

There is a steady increase of the combined or overall amounts of aluminum in a standard car. The increase of cast aluminum is decreasing considerable with the increase of the wrought aluminum contribution with a nearly equal contribution. The figure further implies that there is a continues increase of aluminum share in cars. A proper modeling of this behavior after 2030 because necessary, as this increase can not continue in a similar way into the further future.


### Calculate the ration between the different alloys and the combined amounts

In a first approximation it is assumed that the ratio of the different aluminum alloys stays the same across all the different car segments. 

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# prepare a new data frame

ratioAl.standard <- AlCalculate.standard

# calculate the ratios

ratioAl.standard <- ratioAl.standard %>% group_by(year) %>% mutate(ratioCasting = castingValue/combinedValue)
ratioAl.standard <- ratioAl.standard %>% group_by(year) %>% mutate(ratioExtrusion = extrusionValue/combinedValue)
ratioAl.standard <- ratioAl.standard %>% group_by(year) %>% mutate(ratioForging = forgingValue/combinedValue)
ratioAl.standard <- ratioAl.standard %>% group_by(year) %>% mutate(ratioSheet = sheetValue/combinedValue)

# Calculate the ratio of the combined values as a sum of all the ratios of the individual ratios. It has to be 1 and test, if there is any problem concerning the individual ratios.

ratioAl.standard <- ratioAl.standard %>% group_by(year) %>% mutate(ratioCombined = ratioCasting + ratioExtrusion + ratioForging + ratioSheet)

# rearrange the data.frame, so that it is consitent and better to understand

ratioAl.standard <- ratioAl.standard %>% relocate(segment, .after = last_col())
#ratioAl.standard

```

The figure shows, that the US data are not in line with the European data, even both recent studies were made by Ducker nearly at the same time. Therefore the segment based information will use only the data of aluminum_content_3.


## Interpolate the values from 1980 to 2030 for different car type (length) of total aluminum

### Segment A and JA car (V0101010101 & V0101010201)

The amount of aluminum in a segment A car is shown to be constant from 2020 to 2030. But the trend for the standard car from 1980 to 2030 show a steady increase. Therefore we have to assume that the amount of aluminum in a segment A car flows this trend, but seams to level of for this segment. Hence we will use a trend which follows the overall trend.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

#
## car segment A (V0101010101)

yearCalculate <- c(startDate:2030)

# get all the values of car segment A
temp <- aluminum_content_3 %>% filter(Segment == "A")

# get the value of 2025 to adjust everything and bring it in line
totalAl2025 <- AlCalculate.standard %>% filter(year == 2025)

# model the values (we assume it is a straight line)
ratioSegmentA <- median(temp$totalMass) / totalAl2025$combinedValue

AlCalculate.A <- AlCalculate.standard %>%
                              mutate(totalAlCalculate = combinedValue * ratioSegmentA, castingAlCalculate = castingValue * ratioSegmentA,
                                     extrusionAlCalculate = extrusionValue * ratioSegmentA, forgingAlCalculate = forgingValue * ratioSegmentA,
                                     sheetAlCalculate = sheetValue * ratioSegmentA, segment = "A") %>%
                              select(-castingValue, -extrusionValue, -forgingValue, -sheetValue, -combinedValue)

#AlCalculate.A

g <- ggplot() +
      geom_point(data = AlCalculate.A, mapping = aes(x = year, y = totalAlCalculate), color = "blue") +
      geom_smooth(data = AlCalculate.A, mapping = aes(x = year, y = totalAlCalculate), method = "loess", se = FALSE, linetype = "dashed") +
      ggtitle("Total aluminum alloys for segment A car") +
      xlab("production year") +
      ylab("mass (kg) per car") +
      coord_fixed(ratio = 0.25)  # Adjust the ratio as needed

plot(g)


# Calculate the SUV composition
factor <- derivedSUVComposition %>% filter(segment == "A")

AlCalculate.JA <- AlCalculate.A %>%
                              select(year, totalAlCalculate, castingAlCalculate, extrusionAlCalculate, forgingAlCalculate,
                                     sheetAlCalculate, segment) %>%
                              mutate(year = year, totalAlCalculate = totalAlCalculate * factor$scaleFactor,
                                     castingAlCalculate = castingAlCalculate * factor$scaleFactor,
                                     extrusionAlCalculate = extrusionAlCalculate * factor$scaleFactor,
                                     forgingAlCalculate = forgingAlCalculate * factor$scaleFactor,
                                     sheetAlCalculate = sheetAlCalculate * factor$scaleFactor,
                                     segment = factor$segment_SUV
                                     )
#AlCalculate.JA

```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
      ggtitle("Total aluminum alloys for segment F car") +
      xlab("production year") +
      ylab("mass (kg) per car") +
      coord_fixed(ratio = 0.06)  # Adjust the ratio as needed

plot(g)


# Calcualte the SUV composition
factor <- derivedSUVComposition %>% filter(segment == "F")

AlCalculate.JF <- AlCalculate.F %>%
                              select(year, totalAlCalculate, castingAlCalculate, extrusionAlCalculate, forgingAlCalculate,
                                     sheetAlCalculate, segment) %>%
                              mutate(year = year, totalAlCalculate = totalAlCalculate * factor$scaleFactor,
                                     castingAlCalculate = castingAlCalculate * factor$scaleFactor,
                                     extrusionAlCalculate = extrusionAlCalculate * factor$scaleFactor,
                                     forgingAlCalculate = forgingAlCalculate * factor$scaleFactor,
                                     sheetAlCalculate = sheetAlCalculate * factor$scaleFactor,
                                     segment = factor$segment_SUV
                                     )
```

## Put everything into one table

To be useful everything has to go into one table. Furthermore some rearangements are made, so that the table is better readable and understandable.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Bring the AlCalculate.V01010100 dataset into the same format as all the other ones, so that they can be combined

AlCalculate.standard <- AlCalculate.standard %>% relocate(segment, .after = last_col())  %>%
                          relocate(combinedValue, .after = year) %>%
                          rename(totalAlCalculate = combinedValue,
                                                        castingAlCalculate = castingValue,
                                                        extrusionAlCalculate = extrusionValue,
                                                        forgingAlCalculate = forgingValue,
                                                        sheetAlCalculate = sheetValue)


AlCalculate <- bind_rows(AlCalculate.standard, AlCalculate.A, AlCalculate.B, AlCalculate.C, AlCalculate.D, AlCalculate.E, AlCalculate.F,
                        AlCalculate.JA, AlCalculate.JB, AlCalculate.JC, AlCalculate.JD, AlCalculate.JE, AlCalculate.JF)

AlCalculate <- AlCalculate %>% mutate(productKeyLevel1 = "elvPetrol")

additionalproductKeyLevel1 <- c("elvDiesel", "elvBEV", "elvHEV", "elvPHEV", "elvOther")

# Duplicate the dataset 5 times, each time with a new description
AlCalculate <-  bind_rows(AlCalculate,  # Keep the original dataset
                  map_dfr(additionalproductKeyLevel1, ~ AlCalculate %>%
                  mutate(productKeyLevel1 = .x))
                  )

AlCalculate <- AlCalculate %>% left_join(productKeys, by = c("productKeyLevel1", "segment"))
#AlCalculate
```

# Start combining the new data with the old data for each of the different steels

## castIron

https://metalcastinginstitute.com/cast-iron-automotive-applications 8% of average weight. This is not a to interesting source https://castimoo.com/what-are-the-properties-of-iron-castings-used-in-the-automotive-industry/

Copiplot text In modern cars, cast iron still plays a significant role, especially in components that require high strength and durability. On average, cast iron makes up about **8% of the total vehicle weight**[1](https://metalcastinginstitute.com/cast-iron-automotive-applications/). This includes parts like brake rotors, some brake caliper structures, and occasionally engine components[1](https://metalcastinginstitute.com/cast-iron-automotive-applications/)[2](https://castimoo.com/what-are-the-properties-of-iron-castings-used-in-the-automotive-industry/).

The use of cast iron has slightly declined over the past decade due to the automotive industry's shift towards lighter materials like aluminum. However, it remains essential for parts where its properties, such as wear resistance and thermal conductivity, are crucial[1](https://metalcastinginstitute.com/cast-iron-automotive-applications/)[2](https://castimoo.com/what-are-the-properties-of-iron-castings-used-in-the-automotive-industry/).

There is an interesting article concerning the average weight of cars depending on the continent https://www.measuringknowhow.com/average-car-weight-key-facts-explained/ But this slight decrease is compensated by the overall size and weight increase.

Therefore it is essential to correct the JRC data for the steady increase of the car-weight for all segments and the standard cars, as they are not reflected in the JRC data. For this purpose we use the initial ratio of a given material between 1980 and 1990 towards the overall weight of a car. Based on this assumption we add the yearly increase of weight using this ration towards the overall increase until 2010. Afterwards the JRC corrected data are combined with the new data.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# get the old data
temp_old <- JRC_Data %>% filter(materialKeyLevel2 == "castIron" & is.na(element) & productKeyLevel2 == "V0101010000")

#remove all unnecessary columns
temp_old <-temp_old %>% select(c(productionYear, materialKeyLevel2, value))

# transform a two variable back to numerals
temp_old$productionYear <- as.numeric(temp_old$productionYear)
temp_old$value <- as.numeric(temp_old$value)

# Calculate the average value
temp_old_average <- temp_old %>% filter((productionYear >= 1980) & (productionYear <= 1990)) %>% summarise(avg_value = mean(value))

#Get the ratio
ratiocastIron <- temp_old_average / startWeightCar

## Calculate the annual increase between 1980 and 2010 based on the ratio and annual increase of the weight
# Create a data frame
increasecastIron <- data.frame(year = 1980:2010, value = 0)

# Extract the slope (coefficient) from the model and calculate its ratio
slopecastIron <- coef(modelcarWeightStandard)["Year"] * ratiocastIron$avg_value

# Calculate the new values based on the slope
increasecastIron <- increasecastIron %>% mutate(new_value = value + slopecastIron * (year - 1980))

temp_old <- temp_old %>% mutate(value = value + increasecastIron$new_value)

# Display the corrected JRC data
g <- ggplot() +
      geom_point(data = temp_old, mapping = aes(x = productionYear, y = value), color = "blue") +
      geom_smooth(data = temp_old, mapping = aes(x = productionYear, y = value),  method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "blue") +
      ggtitle("CastIron in a standard car - weight adjusted JRC data") +
      scale_x_continuous(name = "production year") +
      scale_y_continuous(name = "mass (kg)") 

plot(g)

## The adjusted JRC data vary over time. It is best to obtain the average and the use this average values for the whole time-period (1980 to 2030)

# calculate the mean
temp <- temp_old %>% filter(productionYear >= 1980 & productionYear <= 2010)
castIronMean <- mean(temp$value)

# generate the dataset for castIron 2010:2030
year <- c(1980:2030)
values <- rep(castIronMean, times = 51)

castIronCalculate <- data.frame(yearCalculate = year, valueCalculate = values)

# dispaly the combined data

g <- ggplot() +
      geom_point(data = temp_old, mapping = aes(x = productionYear, y = value), color = "black") +
      geom_smooth(data = temp_old, mapping = aes(x = productionYear, y = value),  method = "loess", se = FALSE, span = 0.4, color = "black") +
      geom_point(data = castIronCalculate, mapping = aes(x = yearCalculate, y = valueCalculate), color = "blue") +
      geom_smooth(data = castIronCalculate, mapping = aes(x = yearCalculate, y = valueCalculate),  method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "blue") +
      ggtitle("CastIron in a standard car (averaged value)") +
      scale_x_continuous(name = "production year") +
      scale_y_continuous(name = "mass (kg)", limits = c(0, 210)) 

plot(g)

## combine the two data sets into one and then obtain a smooth function for the overall time period 1980 - 2030
# use the average values
castIronCalculate <- castIronCalculate %>% rename(year = yearCalculate, castingIron = valueCalculate)
#castIronCalculate
```


## mildSteel

One has also to correct in a similar way the JRC data of mild steel, as it was done for the castiron. The JRC data do not consider the overall weight increase of the cars.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# get the old data
temp_old <- JRC_Data %>% filter(materialKeyLevel2 == "mildSteel" & is.na(element) & productKeyLevel2 == "V0101010000")

#remove all unnecessary columns
temp_old <-temp_old %>% select(c(productionYear, materialKeyLevel2, value))

# transform a two variable back to numerals
temp_old$productionYear <- as.numeric(temp_old$productionYear)
temp_old$value <- as.numeric(temp_old$value)

# Calculate the average value
temp_old_average <- temp_old %>% filter((productionYear >= 1980) & (productionYear <= 1990)) %>% summarise(avg_value = mean(value))

#Get the ratio
ratiomildSteel <- temp_old_average / startWeightCar

## Calculate the annual increase between 1980 and 2010 based on the ratio and annual increase of the weight
# Create a data frame
increasemildSteel <- data.frame(year = 1980:2010, value = 0)

# Extract the slope (coefficient) from the model and calculate its ratio
slopemildSteel <- coef(modelcarWeightStandard)["Year"] * ratiomildSteel$avg_value

# Calculate the new values based on the slope
increasemildSteel <- increasemildSteel %>% mutate(new_value = value + slopemildSteel * (year - 1980))

temp_old <- temp_old %>% mutate(value = value + increasemildSteel$new_value)

# Display the weight corrected JRC data
g <- ggplot() +
      geom_point(data = temp_old, mapping = aes(x = productionYear, y = value), color = "blue") +
      geom_smooth(data = temp_old, mapping = aes(x = productionYear, y = value),  method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "blue") +
      ggtitle("CastIron in a standard car - weight adjusted JRC data") +
      scale_x_continuous(name = "production year") +
      scale_y_continuous(name = "mass (kg)") 

plot(g)

# get the new data
temp_new <- steel_combined_long %>% filter((Materials == "mildSteel") & (year > 2010))

g <- ggplot() +
      geom_point(data = temp_old, mapping = aes(x = productionYear, y = value), color = "black") +
      geom_smooth(data = temp_old, mapping = aes(x = productionYear, y = value),  method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "black") +
      geom_point(data = temp_new, mapping = aes(x = year, y = values), color = "blue") +
      geom_smooth(data = temp_new, mapping = aes(x = year, y = values),  method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "blue") +
      ggtitle("MildSteel in a standard car - JRC data (black) & new data (blue)") +
      scale_x_continuous(name = "production year") +
      scale_y_continuous(name = "mass (kg)") 

plot(g)

## Looking at this figure. It becomes obvious that the old and new data fit together. Looking at the comparisons between the actual weight of the different car classes and the calculated one, it becomes obvious, that the gap is too large.

# prepare temp_old and temp_new, so that they can be combined
temp_old <- temp_old %>% filter( productionYear <= 2005)
temp_new <- temp_new %>% select(-Scenario) %>% rename(productionYear = year, materialKeyLevel2 = Materials, value = values)

temp_new <- temp_new %>% filter((value > 280)) %>% mutate(value = value * 1.5)

temp <- bind_rows(temp_old, temp_new)
temp

g <- ggplot() +
      geom_point(data = temp, mapping = aes(x = productionYear, y = value), color = "blue") +
      geom_smooth(data = temp, mapping = aes(x = productionYear, y = value),  method = "loess", se = FALSE, span = 0.4, color = "blue") +
      ggtitle("MildSteel in a standard car - old data (until 2005) & new data (starting 2010)") +
      scale_x_continuous(name = "production year") +
      scale_y_continuous(name = "mass (kg)") 

plot(g)

# start model the new data (interpolate) for the whole time period with available data (1980 - 2025)
yearCalculate <- c(1980:2020)
mildSteelInterpolate <- data.frame(yearCalculate = yearCalculate)

mmildSteelCaculate <- loess(value ~ productionYear, data = temp, span = 0.4) #0.85
valueCalulate <- predict(mmildSteelCaculate, yearCalculate)

mildSteelCalculate <- as.data.frame(cbind(yearCalculate = yearCalculate, valueCalculate = valueCalulate))

# extrapolate to 2030 - it is assume as a first order, that the amount of mild steel only decreases, if it is replaced by other materials
temp <- mildSteelCalculate %>% filter(yearCalculate == 2020)

yearCalculate <- c(2021:2030)

# Create a vector with identical values (e.g., 100)
identical_values <- rep(temp$valueCalculate, length(yearCalculate))

# Combine the vectors into a data frame
df <- data.frame(yearCalculate = yearCalculate, valueCalculate = identical_values)
mildSteelCalculate <- bind_rows(mildSteelCalculate, df)

g <- ggplot() +
      geom_point(data = mildSteelCalculate, mapping = aes(x = yearCalculate, y = valueCalculate), color = "blue") +
      geom_smooth(data =  mildSteelCalculate, mapping = aes(x = yearCalculate, y = valueCalculate),  method = "loess", se = FALSE, span = 0.3, color = "blue") +
      ggtitle("MildSteel in a standard car - Calculated values (1980 - 2030)") +
      scale_x_continuous(name = "production year") +
      scale_y_continuous(name = "mass (kg)") 

plot(g)
```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# get the old data

# transform a two variable back to numerals
temp_old$productionYear <- as.numeric(temp_old$productionYear)
temp_old$value <- as.numeric(temp_old$value)

# Calculate the average value
temp_old_average <- temp_old %>% filter((productionYear >= 1980) & (productionYear <= 1985)) %>% summarise(avg_value = mean(value))

#Get the ratio
ratioHSS <- temp_old_average / startWeightCar

## Calculate the annual increase between 1980 and 2010 based on the ratio and annual increase of the weight
# Create a data frame
increaseHSS <- data.frame(year = 1980:2010, value = 0)

# Extract the slope (coefficient) from the model and calculate its ratio
slopeHSS <- coef(modelcarWeightStandard)["Year"] * ratioHSS$avg_value

# Calculate the new values based on the slope
increaseHSS <- increaseHSS %>% mutate(new_value = value + slopeHSS * (year - 1980))

temp_old <- temp_old %>% mutate(value = value + increaseHSS$new_value)

g <- ggplot() +
      geom_point(data = temp_old, mapping = aes(x = productionYear, y = value), color = "blue") +
      geom_smooth(data = temp_old, mapping = aes(x = productionYear, y = value),  method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "blue") +
      ggtitle("HSS in a standard car - JRC data (blue)") +
      scale_x_continuous(name = "production year") +
      scale_y_continuous(name = "mass (kg)") 

plot(g)

# get the new data
temp_new <- steel_combined_long %>% filter((Materials == "HSS") & (year > 2010))

g <- ggplot() +
      geom_point(data = temp_old, mapping = aes(x = productionYear, y = value), color = "black") +
      geom_smooth(data = temp_old, mapping = aes(x = productionYear, y = value),  method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "black") +
      geom_point(data = temp_new, mapping = aes(x = year, y = values), color = "blue") +
      geom_smooth(data = temp_new, mapping = aes(x = year, y = values),  method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "blue") +
      ggtitle("MildSteel in a standard car - JRC data (black) & new data (blue)") +
      scale_x_continuous(name = "production year") +
      scale_y_continuous(name = "mass (kg)") 

plot(g)

# prepare temp_old and temp_new, so that they can be combined
temp_old <- temp_old %>% filter( productionYear <= 2010)
temp_new <- temp_new %>% select(-Scenario) %>% rename(productionYear = year, materialKeyLevel2 = Materials, value = values)

#remove the values from 2025, as they are unrealisticly low
```

## Magnesium content.  (Still missing - move to front and then reduce amount of Al by 1/3 more than just weight to weight)

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# bring it to longer format, so that handling becomes easier
magnesium_content <- magnesium_content %>% pivot_longer(cols = -c(year, segment), names_to = "drivetrain", values_to = "value")

# calculate the standard magnesium content as mean between c and d segment and the relocate columns, so that it be combined with magnesium_content
magnesium_content_standard <- magnesium_content %>% filter(segment == "C" | segment == "D") %>% group_by(drivetrain, year) %>% summarise(value = mean(value), segment = "standard") %>%
                                relocate(year) %>% relocate(segment, .after = year)

# combine to get everything 
magnesium_content <- bind_rows(magnesium_content, magnesium_content_standard)

magnesiumCalulate <- data.frame(yearCalculate = numeric(), valueCalculate = numeric(), drivetrain = character(), segment = character())

unique_drivetrain <- unique(magnesium_content$drivetrain)
for (i in 1:length(unique_drivetrain)) {
  temp_drivetrain <- magnesium_content %>% filter(drivetrain == unique_drivetrain[i])
  unique_segment <- unique(temp_drivetrain$segment)
  for (j in 1: length(unique_segment)) {
    yearCalculate <- c(1980:2050)
    temp_model <- temp_drivetrain %>% filter((segment == unique_segment[j]) & (value > 0))
    if(dim(temp_model)[1] == 0) {
      valueCalculate <- rep(0, (2050-1980+1))
      tempCalculate <- data.frame(yearCalculate = yearCalculate, valueCalculate = valueCalculate, drivetrain = unique_drivetrain[i],
                                     segment = unique_segment[j])
    }
    else {
      mtempLinear <- lm(value ~ year, data = temp_model)
      summary(mtempLinear)
      
      valueCalculate <- yearCalculate * mtempLinear$coefficients[2] + mtempLinear$coefficients[1]
      tempCalculate <- as.data.frame(cbind(yearCalculate, valueCalculate))
      tempCalculate <- tempCalculate %>% mutate(valueCalculate = replace(valueCalculate, valueCalculate < 0, 0)) %>% mutate(drivetrain = unique_drivetrain[i]) %>%
                          mutate(segment = unique_segment[j])
    }
  
  g <- ggplot() +
          geom_point(data = temp_model, mapping = aes(x = year, y = value)) +  
          geom_point(data = tempCalculate, mapping = aes(x = yearCalculate, y = valueCalculate), color = "blue") +
          geom_line(data = tempCalculate, mapping = aes(x = yearCalculate, y = valueCalculate), method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
          ggtitle(paste("Magnesium alloys for ", magnesium_content$drivetrain[i], " ", unique_segment[j], " car (calculated from 1980 to 2050)")) +
          xlab("production year") +
          ylab("mass (kg) per car")

  plot(g)
  magnesiumCalulate <- bind_rows(magnesiumCalulate, tempCalculate)
  }
}

MgCalculate <- magnesiumCalulate %>% rename(productKeyLevel1 = drivetrain) %>% left_join(productKeys, by = c("productKeyLevel1", "segment")) %>% rename(MgCalculate = valueCalculate)  %>%
                rename(year = yearCalculate)
```

## Combine all the data

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#AlCalculate
#FeCalculate
#MgCalulate

# combine Al and iron, steel
Calculate <- AlCalculate %>% left_join(FeCalculate, by = join_by(year, productKeyLevel1, productKeyLevel2, segment))

# combine with Mg
Calculate <- Calculate %>% left_join(MgCalculate, by = join_by(year, productKeyLevel1, productKeyLevel2, segment))

# the Al and Fe alloys have to be reduced by the amount of Mg alloys used in stead

Calculate <- Calculate %>% mutate(
    ratioFe = MgCalculate / totalIronSteelCalculate)

Calculate <- Calculate %>% mutate(
    castIronCalculate = castIronCalculate * (1 - ratioFe),
    mildSteelCalculate = mildSteelCalculate * (1 - ratioFe),
    HSSCalculate = HSSCalculate * (1 - ratioFe),
    AHSSCalculate = AHSSCalculate * (1 - ratioFe),
    UHSSCalculate = UHSSCalculate * (1 - ratioFe),
    totalIronSteelCalculate = castIronCalculate + mildSteelCalculate + HSSCalculate + AHSSCalculate + UHSSCalculate
) %>% select(-ratioFe)

# calculate the total amount of alloys
```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Look at Pt, Rh & Pd

# get linear behavior between 2009 and 2019

temp <- catalyst_content_1 %>% filter(year > 2008)

calculate.Pt <- mean(temp$Pt)
calculate.Rh <- mean(temp$Rh)

temp <- catalyst_content_1 %>% filter(year > 2009)
tempPd <- temp$Pd

temp <- catalyst_content_1 %>% filter(year > 2012 & year < 2019)
mtempLinear <- lm(Pd ~ year, data = temp)
summary(mtempLinear) 

Pd.2019 <- tempPd[length(tempPd)]

for(i in 1:11) {
  tempPd <- append(tempPd, Pd.2019 + i * mtempLinear$coefficients[2]) 
}

yearCalculate <- c(2010:2030)

PGEcalucalute.V0101010000 <- data.frame(year = yearCalculate, PdCalculate = tempPd/1000, PtCalculate = calculate.Pt/1000, RhCalculate = calculate.Rh/1000, productKeyLevel2 = "V0101010000")
```

Based on the last figures the data, which were derived by Manuele were selected (catalyst_content_2). These values have now to be expanded until 2050

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

last_row <- calalyst_content_2 %>% filter(year == 2023)

years <- 2024:2050
newData <- data.frame(year = rep(years, each = dim(last_row)[1]),
                      standard = rep(last_row$standard, length(years)),
                      A = rep(last_row$A, length(years)),
                      B = rep(last_row$B, length(years)),
                      C = rep(last_row$C, length(years)),
                      D = rep(last_row$D, length(years)),
                      E = rep(last_row$E, length(years)),
                      F = rep(last_row$F, length(years)),
                      drivetrain = rep(last_row$drivetrain, length(years)),
                      Element = rep(last_row$Element, length(years))
                      )
calalyst_content_2 <- bind_rows(calalyst_content_2, newData)

calalyst_content_2 <- calalyst_content_2 %>% mutate(JA = A, JB = B, JC = C, JD = D, JE = E, JF = F) %>% rename(productKeyLevel1 = drivetrain)

calalyst_content_2_long <- calalyst_content_2 %>% pivot_longer(cols = -c(year, productKeyLevel1, Element), names_to = "segment", values_to = "values")
calalyst_content_2_long <- calalyst_content_2_long %>% left_join(productKeys, by = join_by(productKeyLevel1, segment))

calalyst_content_2 <- calalyst_content_2_long %>% pivot_wider(names_from = Element, values_from = values, names_prefix = "calculate")
calalyst_content_2 <- calalyst_content_2 %>% mutate(totalPPR = calculatePt + calculatePd + calculateRh + calculateCe + calculateLa)

Calculate <- Calculate %>% left_join(calalyst_content_2, by = join_by(year, productKeyLevel1, productKeyLevel2, segment))
```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

#EEC_ICEV_content_1

# Combine to component families ()
componentFamilyEEC_ICEV <- EEC_ICEV_content_1 %>% group_by(Type) %>% summarise(total = sum(Mass/1000))
componentFamilyEEC_ICEV <- componentFamilyEEC_ICEV %>% pivot_wider(names_from = Type, values_from = total)

componentFamilyEEC_BEV <- EEC_BEV_content_1 %>% group_by(Type) %>% summarise(total = sum(Mass/1000))
componentFamilyEEC_BEV <- componentFamilyEEC_BEV %>% pivot_wider(names_from = Type, values_from = total)

componentFamilyEEC_HEV <- EEC_HEV_content_1 %>% group_by(Type) %>% summarise(total = sum(Mass/1000))
componentFamilyEEC_HEV <- componentFamilyEEC_HEV %>% pivot_wider(names_from = Type, values_from = total)

componentFamilyEEC_PHEV <- EEC_PHEV_content_1 %>% group_by(Type) %>% summarise(total = sum(Mass/1000))
componentFamilyEEC_PHEV <- componentFamilyEEC_PHEV %>% pivot_wider(names_from = Type, values_from = total)

EED_weight <- EED_weight %>% mutate(elvDiesel = ICEV) %>% rename(elvPetrol = ICEV) %>% rename(elvBEV = BEV) %>% rename(elvPHEV = PHEV) %>% rename(elvHEV = HEV) %>% rename(elvOther = OTHER)
EED_weight_long <- EED_weight %>% pivot_longer(cols = -componentFamily, names_to = "productKeyLevel1", values_to = "values")

developmentEEC <- developmentEEC %>% mutate(elvDiesel = ICEV) %>% rename(elvPetrol = ICEV) %>% rename(elvBEV = BEV) %>% rename(elvPHEV = PHEV) %>% rename(elvHEV = HEV) %>% rename(elvOther = OTHER)
developmentEEC_long <- developmentEEC %>% pivot_longer(cols = -componentFamily, names_to = "productKeyLevel1", values_to = "change")

# Define the range of years (1980 to 2030)
years <- 1980:2030

EED_long <- EED_weight_long %>% left_join(developmentEEC_long, by = c("componentFamily", "productKeyLevel1")) %>% expand_grid(year = years) %>%
          mutate(value = case_when(
            # For years before 2015
           year < 2015 ~ values - (2015 - year) * change * values,
          # For years after 2015 (including 2015)
          year >= 2015 ~ values + (year - 2015) * change * values
      ))

EED_long <- EED_long %>% select(-c(values, change)) %>% mutate(value = ifelse(value < 0, 0, value)) %>%
              mutate(value = ifelse(productKeyLevel1 %in% c("elvBEV", "elvHEV", "elvPHEV") & year < 2000, 0, value))
```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Update Calculate

Calculate <- Calculate %>% left_join(EED, by = join_by(year, productKeyLevel1, productKeyLevel2, segment))
Calculate <- Calculate %>% mutate(totalMetals = totalAlloys + EED_total)
#Calculate

## Add the rest material which is given by the data.frame rest - interpolate, so that there are values for each year

# Reshape to long format
rest_long <- rest %>% pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("elv"), names_to = "value_column", values_to = "value")

# Interpolate missing years for each label and value column
rest_interpolated <- rest_long %>%
  group_by(segment, value_column) %>%  # Treat each label and value column independently
  complete(year = full_seq(rest$year, 1)) %>%  # Fill in all missing years
  mutate(
    value = approx(x = year[!is.na(value)], 
                   y = value[!is.na(value)], 
                   xout = year)$y
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# get the complete dataset
restcomplet <- rest_interpolated %>% pivot_wider(names_from = value_column, values_from = value)

restcomplet_long <- restcomplet %>% pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("elv"), names_to = "productKeyLevel1", values_to = "restFactor")

# Calculate the total amount of different materials
Calculate <- Calculate %>% left_join(restcomplet_long, by = c("year", "productKeyLevel1", "segment"))  %>% mutate(totalOtherMaterilas = restFactor * totalMetals) %>%
                select(-restFactor) %>% mutate(total = totalMetals + totalOtherMaterilas)
```

## Add data from 2031 to 2050, which are identical with the 2030 data

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

data_2030 <- Calculate %>% filter(year == 2030)
#data_2030

years <- 2031:2050

for (i in 1:nrow(data_2030)) {
  new_data <- data_2030 %>% slice(rep(i, length(years))) %>% mutate(year = years)
  Calculate <- Calculate %>% bind_rows(new_data)
}

#Calculate

```
